title: Preferred Stage 2 ION terminal site in Cambridge
subtitle: Brownfield grant for Hespeler Road, Cambridge GO station follow-up, conservation authority agreements and wastewater plant recognition.
overview: The Planning and Works Committee recommended that Council endorse location T1, the existing Ainslie Street transit terminal in downtown Galt, as the preferred south terminal for Stage 2 ION light rail {{vote:m4}}. Staff would carry only that location into the initial business case. Several delegates from Cambridge spoke in support. For residents, this settles where the line would end in Cambridge, though the business case still has to compare options before the project proceeds.

The committee also recommended a tax increment grant of up to $1,299,598 for the redevelopment of 201 and 217 Hespeler Road in Cambridge, to be paid from future property tax growth on the remediated site {{vote:m3}}. It recommended agreements with the Grand River Conservation Authority for non-mandatory services and programs.

Committee members also directed staff to report back in spring 2024 on a Cambridge GO train station, including land acquisition options. The meeting opened with the Grand River Conservation Authority recognizing the Preston Wastewater Treatment Plant with gold for its performance. Council would still need to adopt these recommendations.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended endorsing location T1 (Ainslie Street) as the preferred Stage 2 ION south terminal and directed staff to carry only T1 into the initial business case {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.item: Brownfield tax increment grant, Hespeler Road
decisions.detail: The committee recommended a joint tax increment grant of up to $1,299,598 for 201 and 217 Hespeler Road, Cambridge, financed from future incremental tax revenue after remediation and redevelopment {{vote:m3}}.

The committee recommended authorizing the Commissioner of Planning, Development and Legislative Services to enter into memoranda of understanding with the Grand River Conservation Authority for non-mandatory services and programs, and circulating the report to the provincial ministers, area municipalities and the Authority.
The committee received for information the reports on central transit corridor monitoring and on building permit activity and growth, and approved the other consent items {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Delegates supporting the Ainslie Street terminal cited its closeness to Main Street and downtown businesses, its connections to buses, and investment by downtown developers that they said depends on the LRT.

Staff said T1 performed best on trip time, cost, traffic impacts and fewest properties affected. They said a second downtown station would be only about 500 metres from the terminal and add limited benefit.

On equity, one councillor asked what was learned from Stage 1 displacement and missed station locations. A delegate urged guidelines for accessible and subsidized housing near stations, and staff described work on transportation equity and affordable units in major transit station areas.

On a Cambridge GO station, a delegate asked the committee to link it to LRT planning. Staff said the projects are compatible but should be advanced separately so GO does not delay Stage 2, and noted that GO station development charges would not cover land purchases. Some councillors favoured more attention to GO, and one asked that the Milton line also be considered.
One councillor said they would support the recommendation but thought a more northerly terminal deserved a closer look. Another said earlier concerns had been about timing and costs.
